name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Menefee with large fundraising and outside support
Republican challenger with no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The D+29 lean and Menefee's incumbency, strong fundraising, and unopposed outside support make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, while the Republican challenger has shown no measurable campaign. Markets agree, pricing a Democratic win near 95%.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually weak Democratic margin or a surge of outside spending against Menefee would be the main signal to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-18 is a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat with a D+29 partisan lean. Incumbent Christian Menefee, a Democrat, is running for a full term and has raised about $3.6 million, with roughly $7 million in outside support and no recorded outside opposition. Republican Ronald Whitfield has no reported fundraising or cash on hand.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for the general election, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 95%. The seat is rated Safe Democratic.
